title: Grill — Add Fable 5.2 (round 2: Mythos copy + one clarification)
summary: Round 1 is complete (13/13 answered). Two follow-ups: the **Mythos 5.2 override** changes the Mythos block's copy, and your note on the last question asked what I meant. Everything else is recorded as decided.

proven.text: **Round-1 decisions already recorded:** harness scope = Claude Code + Cursor + fx; Mythos 5.2 = **add**; default = Opus 5.5; picker order = family-grouped; hint copy = `family-standard` (add Fable 5.2, demote Fable 5.1/5, leave multipliers as-is); Cursor migration 084 = **include**; Fable 5.1 plain-variant backfill = **include**; Copilot follow-up = ledger only; fx/Cursor/CLI-floor/verification defaults accepted.

**Mythos 5.2 is Fable 5.2's org-gated twin** — same price, context and effort ladder; approved-org (Project Glasswing) access only. No Cursor/fx/Copilot/Antigravity catalog carries it, so it is Claude Code-only.

sections.title: Mythos block copy
sections.intro: Adding Mythos 5.2 makes it the newest Mythos row. The Fable block already has a demotion pattern; this asks whether the Mythos block should mirror it.

questions.title: With Mythos 5.2 added, how should the Mythos block read?
questions.why: The new top row needs a hint, and Mythos 5.1 is no longer the newest release. The answer decides two or three hint strings.
questions.context: Current hints: Mythos 5.1 = 'Fable 5.1's twin — same capability and cost; requires approved-org (Project Glasswing) access. Uses 2x the usage of Opus.'; Mythos 5 = 'Prior Mythos release — Fable 5's twin; requires approved-org (Project Glasswing) access. Uses 2x the usage of Opus.' You chose `family-standard` for the Fable block: the new row gets the current wording, prior rows get 'Prior'/'Earlier', and the multipliers stay as they are. Mirroring that in the Mythos block means adding 'Prior Mythos release —' to 5.1 and giving 5.2 the twin sentence.

sections.title: Clarification
sections.intro: You asked what the last round-1 question meant. This is the plain version.

questions.title: What I meant: is there a concrete 'done' check outside the repo's model tables?
questions.why: The plan will already add the curated rows, argv mapping, effort/mode maps, picker mirror, Cursor spec/migration, tests and docs. I was asking whether you have a specific acceptance check I can't infer from the repo.
questions.context: Examples of what would count: 'a fresh install shows Fable 5.2 in the New Task picker', 'the pipeline can select it by name', 'profile X must default to it', or 'send me a screenshot of the row'. If the listed scope is the whole definition of done, pick 'Nothing else'.

options.label: Nothing else; the listed scope is the definition of done
options.description: The plan's existing acceptance list is enough.
options.consequence: No extra acceptance work; the plan proceeds with the model-table + tests + docs scope.

options.label: Show Fable 5.2 in the New Task picker on a fresh install
options.description: A manual or e2e picker check.
options.consequence: The plan adds a picker smoke check to the acceptance list (the existing e2e already self-derives the Claude list).

options.label: The pipeline must be able to select Fable 5.2 by name
options.consequence: The plan adds a pipeline-selection check; note the `fable` alias already resolves to 5.2, but a versioned pin is a separate config choice.

options.label: A specific profile or template must default to Fable 5.2
options.description: Tell me which profile in the note.
options.consequence: The plan adds a profile-default change and its test; this is otherwise not part of the model-table work.

options.label: A screenshot/demo of the new row
options.consequence: The plan adds a demo step; no code change.

recommendation.reason: Your round-1 answers cover the full 'supported' contract mapped by the investigation; this is only a catch-all.
